description: Hey! We’re students from Rick Hansen Secondary School on the Theory 6 robotics team. We’re really into coding, engineering, and space, and we’re building an astronaut survival map for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. We love solving tough problems and turning ideas into real projects.
summary: We developed an app that helps astronauts navigate Mars safely. It lets you plan a route between point A and point B for some of the most treacherous parts of Mars! It features a fast, easy-to-use UI to plan routes and get to destinations safely.
details:
TerraMars is a desktop app designed for Mars exploration, built using Rust and the GPUI rendering framework. It allows users (specifically astronauts) to make routes between various landing sites, like the Jezero and Gale craters, while navigating through NASA imagery and terrain maps using an interactive viewer like ‘Google Maps”. One of its best features is the ability to check local conditions on Mars as you switch between Earth UTC and Martian local time, helpful for astronauts to communicate to Earth about what is going on and when. 

Compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux, the app also refreshes NASA-published data in real time, ensuring it always has access to the latest information.

A particularly exciting feature of TerraMars is its offline voice-control mode, which utilizes the voice-vox framework for on-device speech recognition and text-to-speech features. This allows for hands-free navigation and planning without any data uploads, helping users greatly.

TerraMars aims to make Mars mission planning easier by providing rich features like a persistent mission log, a variety of mapping layers, and live rover positions.
